sources.entry: Crypter - Crypter is an innovative, convenient and secure cross-platform crypto app that simplifies secure password generation and management by requiring you to only remember one bit, the MasterPass.

summary.one_liner: Crypter is a cross-platform desktop app (built with Electron) that encrypts files and folders with AES-256-GCM and derives all keys from a single MasterPass you need to remember.
summary.what_it_does: Crypter encrypts and decrypts any file or folder; folders are tarred before encryption. Each encrypted item becomes a .crypto file, which is a tar archive containing the encrypted data and a creds file with the public parameters (IV, auth tag, salt) needed for decryption. Encryption keys are derived with PBKDF2 from a MasterPassKey, which is itself derived from the user's MasterPass, so the MasterPass is never used directly for encryption and is not stored. The app enforces MasterPass rules (minimum 8 characters with upper, lower, digit and special character). Users can export and import MasterPass credentials as a credentials.crypter file to decrypt on another machine. The README states prebuilt binaries exist for macOS, Linux (AppImage) and Windows, and that it is available via Homebrew Cask for macOS.
use_cases: encrypt a single file before storing or sharing it
encrypt a folder into a single .crypto file
generate and manage strong passwords with one memorized MasterPass
move encrypted files to another computer with exported credentials
decrypt files previously encrypted with the same MasterPass
notable: Two-level key derivation: MasterPass to MasterPassKey (PBKDF2, 100000 iterations) to per-file encryption keys (PBKDF2, 50000 iterations), with random credentials per MasterPass set or reset
MasterPassKey is held in a WeakMap inside a closure rather than written to disk
Encrypted files are self-contained .crypto tar archives with a separate public creds file
Credentials export/import workflow for decrypting on a different machine
caveats: Decrypting on another machine or after resetting the MasterPass requires exporting and importing the MasterPass credentials file; a plain MasterPass is not enough, per the README
Per the README, the Keychain-based storage of the MasterPass is a v5.0 goal that was still incomplete (the README asks for PRs to finish it)
The README says JS cannot wipe memory, so MasterPassKey erasure relies on garbage collection
